summary: Kilo CLI (packages/opencode, a fork of OpenCode; core services in packages/core) is a Bun/TypeScript coding agent. Its entrypoint is packages/opencode/src/index.ts (yargs CLI, script name `kilo`); the non-interactive one-shot mode is `kilo run --format json --auto --model provider/model "<prompt>"`, which boots the in-process HTTP server, creates a session rooted at the cwd, streams one JSON event per line, auto-approves permission requests, and exits. Model calls go through the Vercel AI SDK; providers come from JSON config (KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT holds inline config), and a custom provider with npm "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible" plus options.baseURL sends OpenAI chat-completions requests (streaming + tool calls) to the proxy, exactly the way the repo's own CLI subprocess tests do (test/lib/test-provider.ts, test/lib/cli-process.ts). The overlay installs Bun 1.3.14 under /opt/harness/bun, copies the repo to /opt/harness/src, runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, and writes a /opt/harness/bin/kilo shim (symlinked into /usr/local/bin and added via profile.d so `bash -lc` keeps it on PATH) that launches src/index.ts with the same bun flags as the repo's dev/test tooling, with the @opentui/solid preload resolved to an absolute path at build time and offline-safe KILO_DISABLE_* defaults exported so the CLI never fetches models.dev, plugins, or updates.
dockerfile:
ARG BASE=debian:bookworm-slim
FROM ${BASE}

ARG BUN_VERSION=1.3.14
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Only what a bare Debian/Ubuntu userland may be missing; never touch the base's python/node.
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl git unzip bash \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Self-contained Bun runtime under /opt/harness (the CLI is a Bun/TypeScript program).
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(uname -m)"; \
    case "$arch" in x86_64) a=x64 ;; aarch64|arm64) a=aarch64 ;; *) echo "unsupported arch: $arch"; exit 1 ;; esac; \
    mkdir -p /opt/harness/bun/bin /opt/harness/bin /tmp/bun; \
    curl -fsSL "https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v${BUN_VERSION}/bun-linux-${a}.zip" -o /tmp/bun/bun.zip; \
    unzip -q /tmp/bun/bun.zip -d /tmp/bun; \
    mv "/tmp/bun/bun-linux-${a}/bun" /opt/harness/bun/bin/bun; \
    chmod +x /opt/harness/bun/bin/bun; \
    rm -rf /tmp/bun; \
    /opt/harness/bun/bin/bun --version

ENV BUN_INSTALL=/opt/harness/bun
ENV PATH=/opt/harness/bin:/opt/harness/bun/bin:$PATH

# Harness source (build context = repo root) and its locked dependencies.
COPY . /opt/harness/src
RUN cd /opt/harness/src && HUSKY=0 bun install --frozen-lockfile

# `kilo` entrypoint: the CLI's own src/index.ts, launched the way the repo's dev/test tooling launches it
# (bun run --conditions=browser --preload=@opentui/solid/preload src/index.ts). The preload is resolved to an
# absolute path at build time because bun resolves bare --preload specifiers relative to the cwd, and the run
# happens in the task directory. The shim also exports offline-safe defaults (no models.dev fetch, no plugin
# install, no autoupdate/share/telemetry) so the CLI works without network even if the caller sets no env.
# Symlinks + profile.d keep it reachable under `bash -lc` (Debian/Ubuntu /etc/profile resets PATH).
RUN set -eux; \
    cd /opt/harness/src/packages/opencode; \
    preload="$(bun -e 'console.log(Bun.resolveSync("@opentui/solid/preload", process.cwd()))')"; \
    test -f "$preload"; \
    printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' \
      'export KILO_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH="${KILO_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH:-1}"' \
      'export KILO_PURE="${KILO_PURE:-1}"' \
      'export KILO_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS="${KILO_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS:-1}"' \
      'export KILO_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE="${KILO_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE:-1}"' \
      'export KILO_DISABLE_SHARE="${KILO_DISABLE_SHARE:-1}"' \
      'export KILO_DISABLE_SESSION_INGEST="${KILO_DISABLE_SESSION_INGEST:-1}"' \
      'export KILO_DISABLE_PRESENCE="${KILO_DISABLE_PRESENCE:-1}"' \
      'export KILO_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD="${KILO_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD:-1}"' \
      'export KILO_DISABLE_CODEBASE_INDEXING="${KILO_DISABLE_CODEBASE_INDEXING:-1}"' \
      'export KILO_TELEMETRY_LEVEL="${KILO_TELEMETRY_LEVEL:-off}"' \
      'export DO_NOT_TRACK="${DO_NOT_TRACK:-1}"' \
      "exec /opt/harness/bun/bin/bun run --conditions=browser --preload=\"$preload\" /opt/harness/src/packages/opencode/src/index.ts \"\$@\"" \
      > /opt/harness/bin/kilo; \
    chmod +x /opt/harness/bin/kilo; \
    ln -sf /opt/harness/bin/kilo /usr/local/bin/kilo; \
    ln -sf /opt/harness/bun/bin/bun /usr/local/bin/bun; \
    printf '%s\n' 'export PATH=/opt/harness/bin:/opt/harness/bun/bin:$PATH' > /etc/profile.d/kilo-harness.sh; \
    cat /opt/harness/bin/kilo
run_command: set -o pipefail; mkdir -p /out; export XDG_DATA_HOME=/out/xdg/data XDG_STATE_HOME=/out/xdg/state XDG_CACHE_HOME=/out/xdg/cache; export KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT="$(printf '{"enabled_providers":["proxy"],"provider":{"proxy":{"name":"Proxy","id":"proxy","env":[],"npm":"@ai-sdk/openai-compatible","options":{"apiKey":"proxy","baseURL":"%s/v1"},"models":{"gpt-4o":{"id":"gpt-4o","name":"gpt-4o","tool_call":true,"attachment":false,"reasoning":false,"temperature":true,"limit":{"context":200000,"output":32000},"cost":{"input":0,"output":0},"options":{}}}}},"model":"proxy/gpt-4o","small_model":"proxy/gpt-4o","share":"disabled","lsp":false,"formatter":false}' "$PROXY_URL")"; kilo run --format json --auto --dangerously-skip-permissions --model proxy/gpt-4o --title task -- "$TASK" | tee /out/kilo-run.jsonl
check_command: kilo --version && kilo --help >/dev/null && KILO_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH=1 KILO_PURE=1 KILO_AUTH_CONTENT='{}' KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT='{"enabled_providers":["proxy"],"provider":{"proxy":{"name":"Proxy","id":"proxy","env":[],"npm":"@ai-sdk/openai-compatible","options":{"apiKey":"proxy","baseURL":"http://127.0.0.1:1/v1"},"models":{"gpt-4o":{"id":"gpt-4o","name":"gpt-4o","tool_call":true,"limit":{"context":200000,"output":32000},"cost":{"input":0,"output":0}}}}}}' kilo models | grep -q '^proxy/gpt-4o'
notes: Why the previous recipe failed: (1) the check command was executed without the recipe's env list, so KILO_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH was unset and `kilo models` (which loads the provider catalog via packages/core/src/models-dev.ts) tried to GET https://models.dev/api.json offline and died with "Transport error"; yargs then printed help to stderr, which is the help text in the error output. (2) The shim hardcoded packages/opencode/node_modules/@opentui/solid/scripts/preload.js, but the lockfile now uses bun's isolated store (node_modules/.bun/@opentui+solid@.../...), so that path no longer exists. Fixes: the check command sets KILO_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH/KILO_PURE/KILO_AUTH_CONTENT inline, the /opt/harness/bin/kilo shim exports the same offline-safe defaults (overridable) so the CLI never needs the env list to start, and the preload path is resolved at build time with Bun.resolveSync inside packages/opencode. Verified with Docker on an arm64 host: the overlay builds on debian:bookworm-slim and on buildpack-deps:jammy (bun install --frozen-lockfile with HUSKY=0; jammy's python stays 3.10.12); the check_command passes under `bash -lc` with --network none and no env on both images; a full run_command under `bash -lc` in /work against a fake OpenAI chat-completions server at $PROXY_URL succeeded on both images: two streamed POST $PROXY_URL/v1/chat/completions calls carrying 21 tool definitions, the returned `bash` tool call executed (auto-approved), /work/hello.txt created, six JSON events on stdout tee'd to /out/kilo-run.jsonl, session data under /out/xdg, exit 0. Design notes: the AI SDK providers do not read OPENAI_BASE_URL, so the proxy URL is injected via KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT as a custom provider "proxy" using @ai-sdk/openai-compatible (the built-in openai provider would use the Responses API, which the proxy does not speak); OPENAI_BASE_URL/OPENAI_API_KEY are kept in env only as harmless belt-and-braces. Do not set KILO_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG: it stops the agent from reading the task directory's AGENTS.md/instructions. lsp:false and formatter:false mirror the repo's own test env. The model name is arbitrary (the proxy substitutes the real model). On x86_64 hosts without AVX2, swap the bun zip for bun-linux-x64-baseline.
